verbalization: Montelukast and Allergic Rhinitis may be linked through a chain of pharmacological and biological mechanisms. The evidence suggests that Montelukast, as a selective COX-2 inhibitor, may modulate inflammatory pathways, potentially reducing nasal inflammation associated with allergic rhinitis. This is supported by the indirect pathway through Desloratadine, an antihistamine, which is known to treat allergic rhinitis by blocking histamine receptors. The lowest common ancestor of Montelukast and Desloratadine is the class of Organonitrogen Heterocyclic Compounds, indicating a shared chemical structure and possible pharmacological interactions. The indirect causal relationship implies that Montelukast may influence the inflammatory response in a way that could alleviate symptoms of allergic rhinitis, though the exact mechanism remains to be fully elucidated.
